claims.text: ASEAN Weekly Disaster Update Week 32 | 3-9 August 2026 (AHA Centre, posted on ReliefWeb 11 August 2026): 'In the Philippines, the combined effects of the enhanced Southwest Monsoon, Tropical Depression LUIS, and Tropical Cyclone KUJIRA triggered widespread flooding, landslides, and strong winds across Regions I, II, III, IVA, IVB, V, VI, IX, and CAR. According to the NDRRMC, as of 10 August 2026 at 0700H UTC+7, these disasters have affected approximately 586K people (171K families), with about 32.8K people currently displaced, of whom 21.7K are being served in 293 evacuation centres. The events resulted in 8 fatalities, 9 injuries, and 1 missing person... In response, the NDRRMOC alert status was raised to RED, while the NDRRMC activated the Inter-Agency Coordinating Cell and NDRRMC Response Clusters to coordinate ongoing response efforts.'

Flash Update No. 1 - Tropical Cyclone KUJIRA - 5 August 2026 (AHA Centre, ReliefWeb): 'NDRRMC, together with its regional offices and relevant authorities, is currently responding to the Combined Effects of Tropical Cyclone "Luis" and the Enhanced Southwest Monsoon which have affected Regions I, II, III, V, IX, and CAR since 30 July 2026. According to NDRRMC Situation Report No. 2, a total of 41,957 individuals (12,410 families) have been affected, of which 5,818 people (1,821 families) were served in side 14 evacuation centres... The NDRRMOC Alert Status is on BLUE.' The bulletin also records Tropical Storm KUJIRA (local name Maymay) at 65 km/h sustained winds, forecast to make landfall over Ilocos Sur or La Union, with PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals No. 1 and No. 2 raised over Northern Luzon.

PHL: Cyclone - 08-2026 - Philippines Southwest Monsoon enhanced by Tropical Cyclones Maymay and Dolphin (IFRC / Philippine Red Cross, posted on ReliefWeb 13 August 2026): confirms Tropical Depression MAYMAY intensified into Tropical Storm MAYMAY (international name Kujira) by 5 August 2026 and made landfall over the Ilocos Sur-La Union area on 6 August 2026, continuing to weaken while crossing Northern Luzon before its remnant merged with Tropical Cyclone DOLPHIN's larger circulation; the Philippine Red Cross supported local authorities with damage/needs assessment, search and rescue, evacuations, and relief distribution, and reports that 'almost 500 million PHP worth of assistance has been provided' by government agencies and partners, with 'hundreds of evacuation centers... operational.'

GDACS flood event report for the Philippines (event id 1104107, episode 1, overall Green alert, reporting window 17 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC to 19 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC, integrating Copernicus EMS/GloFAS assessment with local media reporting of flooding in Luzon and Mindoro): records 1,076 people displaced and 0 deaths in that window, assessed as low humanitarian impact based on magnitude, exposed population and vulnerability.

claims.text: DSWD DROMIC Report #73 on the Combined Effects of Enhanced Southwest Monsoon and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok (as of 7 September 2026, 6PM) records 2,951,644 families (10,320,947 persons) affected across 6,881 barangays in 11 regions (NCR, CAR, I, II, III, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, V, VI, VIII and IX); 138,932 people (38,686 families) remain displaced -- 54,851 people in 694 evacuation centres and 84,081 staying with relatives or friends -- and 4,523 houses have been damaged (603 totally, 3,920 partially). DROMIC's report series does not carry a casualty count.

claims.text: DSWD DROMIC Report #78 on the Combined Effects of Enhanced Southwest Monsoon and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok (as of 10 September 2026, 6AM) counts 2,972,281 families (10,411,273 persons) affected in 6,899 barangays; 35,478 families (127,354 persons) remain displaced (14,416 families/50,438 persons inside evacuation centres, 21,062 families/76,916 persons outside), down from 138,932 as evacuation centres deactivate, with 4,570 houses damaged (609 totally, 3,961 partially) and PHP 2.51 billion in assistance provided.

AHA Centre Weekly Disaster Update, 31 August-6 September 2026 (published 7 September 2026): citing the latest NDRRMC report, the combined effects of the Southwest Monsoon and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok have affected approximately 9.5 million people (2.9 million families), with 43 fatalities, 18 injuries and 5 people reported missing; around 202,000 people remained displaced, including 89,000 temporarily sheltering in 932 evacuation centres.

claims.text: DSWD DROMIC Report #80 on the Combined Effects of Enhanced Southwest Monsoon and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok (as of 11 September 2026, 6AM): a total of 2,972,396 families (10,411,700 persons) are affected in 6,906 barangays across Regions NCR, CAR, I, II, III, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, V, VI, VIII and IX. There are 14,077 families (49,218 persons) in 618 evacuation centres and 21,094 families (77,006 persons) staying with relatives or friends, for a total displaced population of 35,171 families (126,224 persons) in Regions CAR, I, II, III, CALABARZON and VI. A total of 4,575 houses were damaged (610 totally, 3,965 partially damaged). DROMIC's report series does not carry a casualty count.

description: The combined effects of the enhanced Southwest Monsoon and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok have affected more than 10.4 million people across Luzon, Visayas and the Zamboanga Peninsula since late July 2026. DSWD's DROMIC reporting puts the still-displaced population at about 126,000, while NDRRMC figures relayed by the AHA Centre now put the confirmed toll at 43 deaths, 18 injuries and 5 missing, with the national disaster alert status still at RED.

impact.summary: DSWD's DROMIC Report #80 (as of 11 September 2026, 6AM) counts 2,972,396 families (10,411,700 persons) affected across 6,906 barangays in 11 regions; 126,224 people remain displaced (49,218 in evacuation centres, 77,006 with relatives or friends), down slightly from 127,354, and 4,575 houses have been damaged. DROMIC's report series does not carry a casualty count; the AHA Centre's Weekly Disaster Update for 31 August-6 September 2026, citing NDRRMC, now puts the toll at 43 deaths, 18 injuries and 5 missing -- up sharply from the 8 deaths, 9 injuries and 1 missing recorded as of 10 August -- with the NDRRMOC alert status at RED and the Inter-Agency Coordinating Cell activated. GDACS separately recorded a further Green-alert flood episode across Luzon and Mindoro from 17-19 August 2026, with 1,076 people displaced and no fatalities registered in that window.

name: Southwest Monsoon & Tropical Cyclones Luis/Maymay Floods, Philippines

updates.text: DSWD's DROMIC Report #80 recorded 126,224 people still displaced (down slightly from 127,354) among 10,411,700 people affected. Separately, the AHA Centre's weekly update (citing NDRRMC, 31 Aug-6 Sep) raised the confirmed casualty toll sharply to 43 deaths, 18 injuries and 5 missing, up from 8 deaths, 9 injuries and 1 missing as of 10 August.

DSWD DROMIC Report #78 (10 Sep) now covers Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok combined: 10,411,273 persons affected nationwide, with 127,354 people still displaced, down from 138,932, as evacuation centres deactivate.

DSWD's DROMIC Report #73 recorded a sharp escalation in scope, now covering 11 regions and two further systems (Neneng, Pilandok): 2,951,644 families (10,320,947 persons) affected, up from about 586,000 people on 10 August, with 138,932 displaced (up from 32.8K) and 4,523 houses damaged. DROMIC tracks no casualties; the confirmed toll (8 deaths) is unchanged.

GDACS recorded a further Green-alert flood episode across Luzon and Mindoro from 17-19 August 2026, with 1,076 people displaced and no fatalities in that window, on top of the NDRRMC's cumulative tally relayed by the AHA Centre (10 August) of approximately 586,000 people affected, 32.8K displaced and 8 deaths.
